currentContext.expansion: R K SWAMY's expansion in FY2025-26 was footprint and platform build-out rather than plant capex, framed by management as a deliberate transition toward asset-light and technology-driven service layers. The Company commissioned a new state-of-the-art Customer Experience Centre ('CEC') adding 600 additional seats — a capacity increase of nearly 50% — with utilisation at 83% as of March 31, 2026 and management tracking it to surpass 90% in early FY27 on the back of secured client pipelines, which it says directly enhances operating margins. To support the full-service market research division (Hansa Research), it added 346 calling stations to its Computer-Aided-Telephonic-Interviews ('CATI') facility, an 86% capacity increase, enabling rapid, high-volume, multi-regional consumer surveys to run simultaneously. A new Brand and Marketing Consulting Group was launched in the first quarter of FY2025-26 with a full team in place, consolidating brand strategy, consumer insights and market research, digital experience, communications and data analytics under one roof to engage C-suites and founders. The next step is backward integration into content production: the Company has signed a Letter of Intent to lease premium studio space in South Bombay for a dedicated digital video studio to create multi-format, multi-lingual digital video content at scale, cutting client turnaround times and retaining production margins previously outsourced. Management states the Company entered the new fiscal year with upgraded capacity. The Company had 330 permanent employees on its rolls as on March 31, 2026.

risks.risk: Dependence on discretionary client marketing budgets that reset each year
risks.note: The Company states it derives its revenues from the marketing budgets of leading private companies, major Institutions of India, public sector enterprises, multinational companies and Indian brands, and that these budgets 'get refreshed every year'. Revenue therefore has to be re-won annually and is exposed to any cyclical or discretionary cut in client marketing spend.

risks.risk: Concentration of revenue in digital services
risks.note: The Company derived almost 75% of its consolidated revenues from digital services, so group revenue and its high-margin, technology-first model are tied to the continued shift of client spend to digital channels and to the Company keeping pace with digital delivery capability.

risks.risk: Business concentrated in three service pillars
risks.note: Momentum is stated to come from client retention and new business development across three core pillars — Integrated Marketing Communications, Customer Data Analytics & MarTech (Hansa Cequity) and Full-Service Market Research (Hansa Research) — leaving limited diversification if any one discipline loses client traction.

risks.risk: Reliance on unlisted material subsidiaries for group operations
risks.note: Hansa Research Group Private Limited, Hansa Customer Equity Private Limited and Hansa Direct Private Limited are identified as the Company's material subsidiaries and are subject to separate secretarial audit under Regulation 24A(1); a material part of group performance and compliance exposure therefore sits outside the listed entity.

risks.risk: Risk framework is policy-based rather than an enumerated risk register in this report
risks.note: The Board has constituted a Risk Management Committee and adopted a Risk Management Policy, with major risks identified by businesses and functions 'systematically addressed through review and mitigating actions on a continuing basis' and the Audit Committee holding additional oversight of financial risk and controls; the report itself does not enumerate the specific risk factors, limiting external visibility on which exposures management ranks highest.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: R K SWAMY is an independent Indian integrated marketing services group offering a single-window solution spanning communication, media, customer data analytics & MarTech and full-service market research.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: R K SWAMY operates as an integrated marketing communications and business transformation group, providing end-to-end solutions across strategy, creative, media, brand and marketing consulting, data analytics, market research, customer experience and marketing technology. Its services span brand and marketing consulting, branding and design, advertising and creative services, media planning and buying, digital marketing, brand activation, customer experience management, market research, analytics, CRM and marketing technology solutions, delivered to leading private companies, major Indian institutions, public sector enterprises, multinational companies and ambitious Indian brands. Through its subsidiaries Hansa Research and Hansa Cequity, the Company provides market intelligence, customer experience measurement, analytics, CRM strategy, customer engagement and marketing technology solutions.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's advertising industry continues to demonstrate growth momentum, supported by rising consumption, rapid digital adoption and expanding media choices, with favourable demographics and rising disposable incomes
- Demand for advertising and marketing services is broad-based, with FMCG, retail, e-commerce and BFSI the largest contributors to marketing expenditure while automotive, technology, consumer services and digital-first businesses increase customer-acquisition and brand-building spend
- Structural underpenetration of marketing spend — industry studies indicate Indian companies spend approximately 3%-4% of revenue on marketing versus 10%-11% in the United States and Europe, presenting a significant long-term growth opportunity
- Consumer engagement is shifting toward video-led formats, increasing demand for high-quality content creation, data-driven audience targeting and integrated campaign execution across digital platforms
- As marketing becomes data-led, technology-enabled and outcome-oriented, clients are seeking partners capable of providing integrated solutions; firms combining domain expertise with digital capabilities, data assets and scalable execution platforms are expected to be well positioned
- Consolidation among large multinational advertising holding companies may lead to client and talent realignments, creating opportunities for R K SWAMY
- Acceleration of Artificial Intelligence is changing how brands engage with agencies — a challenge management flags for those who treat it as a substitute for human intelligence
- Uncertainties from supply chain disruptions and higher oil prices have shifted client focus toward immediate result-driven digital metrics over traditional long-term brand building
- Revenues are drawn from client marketing budgets that get refreshed every year, described by management as a rich, recurring stream
- Operating leverage — revenue growth outpacing the increase in operating expenses — plus rapid absorption of newly added CEC capacity as margin levers
- CEC utilisation stood at 83% as of March 31, 2026 and is actively tracking to surpass 90% in early FY27 based on secured client pipelines
- Projects undertaken during the year for over 500+ diverse clients, with revenue drawn from annually refreshed marketing budgets of private companies, major Indian institutions, public sector enterprises and multinationals

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Deliberate transition toward asset-light and technology-driven service layers through structural investments made over the last few quarters
- Scale up the Customer Experience Centre (CEC) and drive rapid absorption of the added capacity, which management says directly enhances operating margins
- Build advanced market research infrastructure by expanding the CATI facility to execute rapid, high-volume, multi-regional consumer surveys simultaneously
- Grow the newly launched Brand and Marketing Consulting Group, structured to engage higher up the corporate value chain with C-suites and founders, consolidating brand strategy, consumer insights, digital experience, communications and data analytics under a single window
- Backward-integrate into video content production by establishing a dedicated digital video studio, cutting client turnaround times and retaining production margins previously outsourced
- Operate a technology-first model with digital services contributing approximately 75% of consolidated revenues
- Compete as an independent, locally anchored Indian integrated marketing services group offering clients a stable, execution-focused alternative as global holding companies consolidate, while attracting talent seeking stability and growth
- Simplify execution for clients through a unified single-platform service model integrating strategy, consulting, creative, media, data, research and technology
- Master AI as a tool rather than a substitute for human intelligence in client engagement
- The Company returns cash to shareholders through an annual final dividend put to members for approval — for the year ended March 31, 2026 the AGM notice places before members an ordinary resolution to declare a final dividend of Rs. 2 per equity share (40% of the Rs. 5 face value). The Company has no joint ventures or associates, and its operating structure is held entirely through wholly owned subsidiaries (100% shareholding in each), with the overseas businesses in Dubai and Bangladesh held as step-down subsidiaries of Hansa Customer Equity Private Limited. Non-executive independent directors are remunerated through commission and sitting fees within limits approved by members and in accordance with the Nomination, Remuneration and Board Diversity Policy.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: R K SWAMY's expansion in FY2025-26 was footprint and platform build-out rather than plant capex, framed by management as a deliberate transition toward asset-light and technology-driven service layers. The Company commissioned a new state-of-the-art Customer Experience Centre ('CEC') adding 600 additional seats — a capacity increase of nearly 50% — with utilisation at 83% as of March 31, 2026 and management tracking it to surpass 90% in early FY27 on the back of secured client pipelines, which it says directly enhances operating margins. To support the full-service market research division (Hansa Research), it added 346 calling stations to its Computer-Aided-Telephonic-Interviews ('CATI') facility, an 86% capacity increase, enabling rapid, high-volume, multi-regional consumer surveys to run simultaneously. A new Brand and Marketing Consulting Group was launched in the first quarter of FY2025-26 with a full team in place, consolidating brand strategy, consumer insights and market research, digital experience, communications and data analytics under one roof to engage C-suites and founders. The next step is backward integration into content production: the Company has signed a Letter of Intent to lease premium studio space in South Bombay for a dedicated digital video studio to create multi-format, multi-lingual digital video content at scale, cutting client turnaround times and retaining production margins previously outsourced. Management states the Company entered the new fiscal year with upgraded capacity. The Company had 330 permanent employees on its rolls as on March 31, 2026.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Ability to seamlessly integrate strategy, consulting, creative, media, data, research and technology within a single platform, giving clients one unified partner for brand building, customer acquisition, customer retention and business transformation
- Single-window solution across Communication, Media, Customer Data Analytics & MarTech and Full Service Market Research — described as one of the leading Integrated Marketing Services groups in India
- Technology-first, high-margin model in which digital services contribute approximately 75% of consolidated revenues
- Scale infrastructure — expanded Customer Experience Centre and CATI facility enabling rapid, high-volume, multi-regional consumer surveys and campaign execution
- Proprietary data assets at scale, including a large base of unique customer profiles and private cloud infrastructure supporting one-to-one customer intelligence campaigns
- Broad, renewing client base — projects undertaken for over 500+ clients, with revenues drawn from marketing budgets that get refreshed every year
- Positioned as an independent, locally anchored Indian alternative at a time when global advertising holding companies are consolidating, creating client and talent realignment opportunities
- Licensed use of the established 'R K SWAMY', 'Hansa' and 'Hansa Bird Logo' brands, with the promoter group company having waived its royalty entitlement till FY2026-27
- Debt-free balance sheet — the Company did not have any borrowings during the year and no interest expense was incurred on borrowings

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Dependence on discretionary client marketing budgets that reset each year — The Company states it derives its revenues from the marketing budgets of leading private companies, major Institutions of India, public sector enterprises, multinational companies and Indian brands, and that these budgets 'get refreshed every year'. Revenue therefore has to be re-won annually and is exposed to any cyclical or discretionary cut in client marketing spend.
- Concentration of revenue in digital services — The Company derived almost 75% of its consolidated revenues from digital services, so group revenue and its high-margin, technology-first model are tied to the continued shift of client spend to digital channels and to the Company keeping pace with digital delivery capability.
- Business concentrated in three service pillars — Momentum is stated to come from client retention and new business development across three core pillars — Integrated Marketing Communications, Customer Data Analytics & MarTech (Hansa Cequity) and Full-Service Market Research (Hansa Research) — leaving limited diversification if any one discipline loses client traction.
- Reliance on unlisted material subsidiaries for group operations — Hansa Research Group Private Limited, Hansa Customer Equity Private Limited and Hansa Direct Private Limited are identified as the Company's material subsidiaries and are subject to separate secretarial audit under Regulation 24A(1); a material part of group performance and compliance exposure therefore sits outside the listed entity.
- Risk framework is policy-based rather than an enumerated risk register in this report — The Board has constituted a Risk Management Committee and adopted a Risk Management Policy, with major risks identified by businesses and functions 'systematically addressed through review and mitigating actions on a continuing basis' and the Audit Committee holding additional oversight of financial risk and controls; the report itself does not enumerate the specific risk factors, limiting external visibility on which exposures management ranks highest.
